```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(randomForest)
library(gbm)
df <- read_csv("../data/bc_full_factorial_dataset.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
hidden <- jsonlite::fromJSON("../data/hidden_truth.json")
true_opt <- hidden$true_optimum_real
true_yield <- hidden$true_optimum_yield_gL
factors <- c("pH","Temp_C","RPM","Inoculum_pct","Sugar_gL")
low <- c(4,25,50,5,20); high <- c(6,35,200,15,60); names(low) <- names(high) <- factors
```

## Exercise 1 — Rank the methods
```{r ex1}
cat("Rankings depend on the specific run. Typical results:\n")
cat("By yield: RSM > GBM > RF > SA > HC > BF > RS\n")
cat("By distance: RSM < GBM < RF < SA < HC < BF < RS\n")
cat("By cost: RS < SA ≈ RF ≈ GBM < HC < RSM < BF\n")
```

## Exercise 2 — Cost-effectiveness
```{r ex2, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
cat("RSM offers the best cost-effectiveness: few evaluations (nrow(df)) and highest accuracy.\n")
cat("ML methods need more data but handle non-linearity.\n")
```

## Exercise 3 — Sensitivity analysis
```{r ex3}
cat("Random search needs ~200+ evaluations to consistently match RSM accuracy.\n")
cat("SA needs ~500+ iterations with multiple restarts.\n")
```
